title: LRHE reviewer run record
description: One record per reviewer invocation. Several fields exist purely so a promotion gate can be measured rather than asserted. Every boolean hard gate is REQUIRED: absent telemetry is a failure, not a pass, and `unknown` is not `false`. Adopted before the first real run, so there is no v1 data to migrate -- do not re-loosen this to accommodate a generator that has not been updated.

experiment_id.description: scoring and analysis refuse to run across more than one. The original three-family result set is a different experiment from the OpenCode floor panel and must never be silently pooled with it

panel_id.description: a family comparison is only meaningful within one complete, declared panel

item_id.description: the corpus item under review. There is deliberately no separate review_id: the ledger coalesces review_id -> item_id -> run_id, so on a production run against real work rather than a corpus item, set this to the review's own id. Adding a parallel field would let the two disagree, and the ledger would have to guess which one the finding belongs to

arm.description: defined in panels.yaml, not here. R = cold refutation: unlike A-D it is scheduled per disputed claim rather than per item, so it costs nothing on reviews where nothing is disputed

family.description: stable lineage id, deliberately short: gpt, claude, gemini, grok, kimi, glm, minimax, deepseek. The vendor prefix adds nothing a lineage id needs; route and model identity are separate fields under `reviewer`, which is the distinction that actually matters. Adding families scales arms C/D linearly and inflates 'unique verified findings' by pure arithmetic -- grow arm T with the council or section 7's warning bites harder

lens.description: vocabulary lives in panels.yaml. A closed enum here silently drops whatever a later panel adds -- the handoff's own draft dropped `independent` and `refuter`, both of which this harness schedules

role.description: derivable from arm via panels.yaml; recorded when the emitter knows it. The council is asymmetric, and conflating roles is what makes six families look like six votes when it is four first-pass critics, one conditional refuter and one accountable integrator

replicate.description: set1..setN for arm D, rep1..repN for arm T. Part of the condition key: drop it and N independent runs of one family collapse into a single cell, which deletes the empirical null while still printing the number

artifact_digest.description: what the reviewer actually saw. A run whose digest no longer matches the packet is stale, not comparable

assignment_manifest_digest.description: ties the run to the frozen matrix that scheduled it

requested_model.description: the pinned selector that was asked for

served_model.description: what the provider reported serving. Mismatch or absence is a silent fallback and a hard gate failure; a Fable request answered by Opus is an Opus result

product_route.description: which product or tier of the provider served this. Section 7 wrote it as opencode-go|opencode-zen because it was drafted for the OpenCode expansion, and a two-value enum forced every other route to record one of them -- a Claude run was being stamped `opencode-zen`, a fabricated provenance field on three of the five configured routes. `unknown` is legal; guessing is not

billing_route.description: who is billed this request. `unknown` means the signal was unavailable and is legal; absence is illegal, and inference is forbidden -- a fabricated billing route reconciles against the dashboard and nobody looks again

list_cost_estimate_usd.description: token-derived list price. Record alongside the observed allowance delta, never instead of it: they disagree, and only one of them is billing

quota_pool.description: which allowance the call was charged to. Capture both dashboards around a canary before trusting this

raw_output_digest.description: sha256 digest of the provider's raw output artifact

tool_trace_digest.description: sha256 digest of captured tool trace provenance

telemetry_complete.description: the emitter asserting it captured every field below. False means the run is unscoreable, not that it passed the parts that were captured

tool_violations.description: attempted calls outside the allowlist. Headless task agents run at approval mode yolo, so a prompt saying 'do not edit' is not a control -- this counter is

consumed_peer_output.description: independence violation; round one must be blind

repo_digest_after.description: the measurement behind wrote_to_repo. A reviewer that mutated the tree and reported otherwise is caught here and nowhere else

timed_out.description: a timed-out reviewer is MISSING, never APPROVED

evidence.description: raw contract strings: R<ID>|P<0-3>|conf=..|claim=..|evidence=..|impact=..|verify=.. -- an empty array is a legitimate result, and on an S5 null item it is the correct one

input_rights_record_id.description: foreign key to data_rights.record_id for the decision used by this run

clarification_snapshot_id.description: snapshot id for provider documentation clarifications that arrive after terms snapshotting

provider_documentation_snapshot_id.description: snapshot id of provider documentation for the run-level claims in this run

router_dataset_example_ids.description: row ids in the router-ready dataset derived from this run

allOf.$comment: Claiming verified identity commits you to the evidence for it.
Incomplete telemetry cannot also be a clean run. This is the fail-closed rule expressed in the schema rather than left to the scorer, so a record that lies about itself does not validate.
